stem: A 4-year-old boy is being evaluated for failure to thrive, shortness of breath, and exercise intolerance.  Cardiac examination shows bounding peripheral pulses and a palpable thrill below the left clavicle, where a continuous murmur is also heard.  After discussion with the parents, the patient undergoes surgical correction.  A derivative of which of the following embryonic structures was most likely ligated during the procedure?​‌​‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​​​‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​​​
explanation:
This patient with bounding peripheral pulses and a continuous murmur near the left infraclavicular region most likely has a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA), an embryonic aortic arch derivative.

The aortic arches are paired vascular structures, each associated with a pharyngeal arch in early gestation.  The ductus arteriosus derives from the distal portion of the left sixth aortic arch.  In fetal life, the ductus carries blood from the pulmonary artery to the proximal descending aorta, diverting flow away from the unexpanded lungs.

After birth, increased arterial oxygen tension and decreased prostaglandin E2 (due to placental separation) result in constriction of ductal smooth muscle, producing functional closure within 24–48 hours, with subsequent fibrosis into the ligamentum arteriosum over the ensuing weeks.

Because systemic pressure exceeds pulmonary pressure after birth, the shunt reverses and blood flows left to right from the aorta into the pulmonary artery.  When the ductus fails to close, this persistent flow produces the characteristic continuous "machinery-like" murmur and a palpable thrill below the left clavicle.  Diastolic runoff into the pulmonary circulation also lowers aortic diastolic pressure while the increased stroke volume (due to excess preload from shunted blood) raises systolic pressure, producing bounding pulses (ie, wide pulse pressure).  Sustained pulmonary overcirculation and left ventricular volume overload eventually cause heart failure symptoms to develop (eg, failure to thrive, exercise intolerance).

In preterm infants, the ductus remains prostaglandin-dependent, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (eg, indomethacin) can close it by inhibiting cyclooxygenase and thereby reducing PGE2 synthesis.  However, this approach is ineffective beyond early infancy, and older patients often require transcatheter closure or surgical ligation.

(Choice A)  The bulbus cordis contributes to formation of the right ventricle and the ventricular outflow tracts, including the smooth outflow portions of the right and left ventricles (conus arteriosus and aortic vestibule, respectively).

(Choice B)  The left fourth aortic arch forms the segment of the aortic arch between the left common carotid and left subclavian arteries.  Aortic coarctation can produce a systolic murmur and, when collateral vessels are prominent, continuous murmurs over the back; femoral pulses are typically diminished and delayed relative to brachial pulses rather than bounding.

(Choices C and D)  In the embryonic heart, blood flows from the sinus venosus to the primitive atrium and then the primitive ventricle.  The sinus venosus develops into the smooth portion of the right atrium (sinus venarum) and coronary sinus, whereas the primitive atrium develops into the rough, trabeculated portions of both atria.

Educational objective:The ductus arteriosus, a derivative of the distal left sixth aortic arch, shunts fetal blood from the pulmonary artery to the descending aorta and normally closes after birth.  A patent ductus produces left-to-right shunting with a continuous murmur in the left infraclavicular region and bounding pulses.  Prolonged pulmonary overcirculation and left ventricular volume overload can eventually lead to heart failure.​‌​‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​​​‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​​​
